title: "Visualize saved evidence: curves, uncertainty, stability and SHAP"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette

  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Visualize saved evidence: curves, uncertainty, stability and SHAP}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

The visualization interfaces return ordinary `ggplot2` objects. They do not
choose a winning pipeline, refit a model, invent missing confidence intervals,
or replace saved performance metrics. Plotting requires the optional `ggplot2`
package, not a new mandatory modeling dependency.

## Run the complete synthetic example

This installed example creates **19 plots**, including all five Meta-analysis
types and a fixed-horizon survival example. It uses the core modeling
dependencies plus `ggplot2` and `metafor` (to compute the Meta results).
The forest plotting function itself does not require `metafor` when results
have already been saved. All data are synthetic and are not clinical
evidence. The 40 bootstrap draws keep the tutorial fast, not research-grade.

```{r full-example, eval=FALSE}
library(stormbreaker)
source(system.file("examples", "visualization-core.R", package = "stormbreaker"))
example <- stormbreaker_visualization_example()
print(example$plots$ROC_by_assessment_fold)
print(example$plots$Meta_Discrimination)

# Optional: supply a NEW directory for PNG figures and an offline HTML gallery.
example <- stormbreaker_visualization_example("my-new-visualization-gallery")
```

## Binary ROC and precision-recall curves

```{r binary-curves, fig.width=9, fig.height=7}
library(stormbreaker)
d <- bi_example(80, seed = 401)
task <- bi_task(d, "patient_id", "outcome", c("gene_a", "gene_b", "gene_c"))
pipeline <- sb_pipeline(selector = "univ_binary_auc_top_k", learner = "logistic",
                        selector_n_features = 2L)
cv <- run_cv(task, pipeline, folds = 3L, seed = 402)
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) print(plot_roc(cv))
```

`plot_pr(cv)` uses grouped probability ties and vertical-then-horizontal
steps. The corresponding within-fold area is noninterpolated average precision.
Assessment folds are distinct panels, including inside repeated CV, IECV and
stacking. External cohorts remain distinct. These are descriptive threshold
curves, not pooled replacements for the saved fold-aware AUC/AP estimand.
Invalid groups remain in the `stormbreaker_curve_status` attribute rather than
having bad rows silently removed. `stormbreaker_saved_metrics` retains the
original summaries. This is not a time-dependent survival ROC interface.

## Cohort-by-model performance

```{r heatmap, eval=FALSE}
plot_heatmap(example$evaluations, "roc_auc")
plot_heatmap(example$survival_evaluation, "ipcw_brier")
```

Cells retain saved values. Failed or unavailable cells are not zero-filled;
unsupplied model/cohort combinations are labeled. Task, prediction horizon,
unit, scope and aggregation remain separate. The legend indicates whether
higher or lower values are better. No best model is selected.

## External uncertainty and Meta-analysis

```{r intervals, eval=FALSE}
plot_ext_ci(example$bootstraps, "roc_auc")
plot_ext_diff(example$paired, "roc_auc")
plot_ext_ci(example$survival_bootstrap, "ipcw_brier_score")
plot_forest(example$meta$Discrimination)
plot_forest(example$meta$Calibration_slope)
plot_forest(example$meta$Mean_calibration)
plot_forest(example$meta$Discrimination_difference)
plot_forest(example$meta$Prediction_error_difference)
```

Intervals are copied from saved outputs without new bootstrap draws. Cohort
bootstrap interval metric names are used exactly as saved: for example,
`ipcw_brier_score` in bootstrap outputs versus `ipcw_brier` in result views.
Cohort
bootstrap confidence intervals, pooled confidence intervals and between-cohort
prediction intervals have different labels. A cohort without a saved interval
does not acquire one from its standard error. Successful/requested draw counts
and incomplete status remain visible. Differences mean **candidate minus
reference**: positive differences favor the candidate only for higher-is-better
metrics. Bootstrap uncertainty is conditional on locked predictions, not the
uncertainty from developing the model. Three cohorts give weak information about
heterogeneity; heed the source object's small-cohort caution.

## Feature-selection stability

```{r stability, fig.width=9, fig.height=6}
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) print(plot_freq(cv))
```

```{r stability-more, eval=FALSE}
plot_jaccard(cv)
plot_upset(cv)
# With a supported glmnet CV result and saved active-set records:
# plot_freq(glmnet_cv, source = "glmnet_active_set")
```

Frequency uses the actual successful-fold denominator. Jaccard displays saved
fold pairs only, without invented diagonal entries. The UpSet-style display
counts exact intersections among successful folds within each saved entry;
never-selected features lie outside the selected union. Top-N truncation does
not discard the full intersection table in `stormbreaker_intersections`.
There is no cross-repeat pooling. A non-applicable selector produces an
explicit no-results display, not fabricated stability.

## Existing additive SHAP

```{r shap, eval=FALSE}
plot_shap_imp(example$explanation)
plot_shap(example$explanation)
plot_shap_one(example$explanation, row = 1L, top_n = 2L)
```

The beeswarm is deterministic and does not change random state. Without
explicitly ID-aligned feature values, points use a single color. Waterfalls
retain the background reference, displayed terms, the sum of omitted terms,
and the reconstructed score. Contributions remain on the saved log-odds or
log-hazard scale, **not probability changes and not causal effects**. This API
visualizes supported additive explanations; it is not generic black-box SHAP.
Original patient identifiers are excluded from the plot data, but individual
values can still be sensitive.

## Export and inspect

```{r export, eval=FALSE}
p <- example$plots$SHAP_waterfall
p$data                         # inspect plotted numbers locally
ggplot2::ggsave("new-waterfall.pdf", p, width = 12, height = 7)
sb_render_visual_report(example$plots, "new-gallery.html", width = 12, height = 9)
```

Choose new output paths and review visible labels and points before sharing.
The HTML gallery is a single offline file with embedded SVG images, without
raw result objects or patient tables; it is not an anonymization service.
Use larger dimensions for many cohorts/folds. For scalar tables, calibration,
decision curves and failure records, the existing `sb_render_report()` remains
available unchanged.
